newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL-Sweden's CPI seen rising 0.1 pct m/m in July.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Sweden's CPI seen rising 0.1 pct m/m in July.

text.p: Sweden's consumer price index is expected to show a rise of 0.1 percent in July for a year-on-year increase of 1.2 percent, a Reuters poll of 16 analysts forecast on Thursday.
Forecasts varied between a drop of 0.1 percent to a rise of 0.4 percent for the month to give a year-on-year figure of between 0.9 and 1.5 percent.
In June the CPI rose 0.1 percent for a year-on-year increase of 0.8 percent. In July 1996 it fell 0.2 percent, which gave an annual rate of 0.6 percent.
For the full 1997 year the average of 13 analysts' forecasts tipped a 1.0 percent rise in the CPI. Forecasts varied between 0.6 and 1.3 percent. In 1996 the CPI rose an average 0.8 percent.
Statistics Sweden will release July CPI data on August 19 at 0715 GMT.

Analysts surveyed for the poll were from Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, IDEA, JP Morgan, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley, Penser, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, UBS and Unibank Markets.
Annual forecasts were not given by Consensus, Penser and PaineWebber.
